Worst Car-Buying Experience I’ve HadMy experience with Cars24 left me feeling that the company prioritizes lead generation and sales metrics over honesty, transparency, and customer experience.I found a Nissan on the Cars24 app and was subsequently bombarded with automated calls and follow-up calls from sales representatives. I was told that although the exact vehicle I wanted was located far away, there were 3 of the same models available at a Cars24 location near me. An appointment was scheduled for 12:00 PM, and I was encouraged to visit that location.I was shopping for a vehicle for my daughter, who had just arrived in India and was preparing to start school. We were excited about the process and arrived on time for our appointment.Unfortunately, the experience quickly deteriorated.From the front entry glass doors, the office itself appeared disorganized. Several sales staff were gathered near the entrance chatting while other employees seemed occupied with unrelated matters. After walking into the front door, I explained that I had an appointment to view a specific vehicle.To my surprise, I was told the vehicle was not available at that location. When I showed the appointment confirmations and text messages I had received, the representative admitted that the call center often schedules appointments simply to get customers into a showroom, hoping they will purchase something else once they arrive.Think about that for a moment.A customer is told a vehicle is available, takes time out of their day, travels to the location, and only then learns that the appointment was essentially a lead-generation tactic.As the conversation continued, the focus immediately shifted to whether I would be paying cash or financing the vehicle. At no point did anyone attempt to understand my needs, budget, intended use, or what would be important for my daughter as a first-time driver.When I asked again about the Nissan model I had originally come to see, another employee casually mentioned that it had been sold earlier that day. I was then shown alternative listings on a tablet and told that if I wanted to see one of the vehicles located elsewhere, I would first need to pay a ₹15,000 registration fee to have it brought over.By that point, it was clear that the appointment I had been promised was never going to happen.The most disappointing part was not that the vehicle was unavailable. Cars get sold every day. The problem was the lack of honesty, transparency, and respect for a customer’s time.Cars24 heavily markets concepts such as trust, peace of mind, fair pricing, and customer satisfaction. My experience reflected the opposite:• Misleading appointment scheduling• Unprofessional sales tactics• Poor communication between the call center and showroom staff• Little interest in understanding customer needs• A process that felt focused on capturing leads rather than helping customersI hope senior management takes these concerns seriously because experiences like this damage trust far more than any marketing campaign can rebuild it.
